docs.task: How the native loop counts tool calls and accumulates usage for a run.

asks: Explain how the native loop counts tool calls
Explain how the native loop accumulates usage for a run

data_flow.step: NativeExecutor::run creates `usage = Arc<Mutex<Usage::default()>>` and moves a clone into `Run`. It races `run.execute()` against cancel and a timeout of spec.timeout_secs; on cancel or timeout it cancels the inner token, waits CLEANUP_GRACE, and returns a result with `usage = *usage.lock()`.

execute loops up to MAX_TURNS. Each iteration builds a ChatRequest and, if the estimated context reaches COMPACT_AT of the window and the last message is a user turn, calls compact, which calls add_usage(&out.usage, vec![]) so compaction cost joins the total as a Turn with no call ids.

After each provider response, `usage = resp.usage; usage.context_tokens = context_of(&usage)` (input + cache read + cache write + output). `call_ids` are the ids of every tool_use block in the response, including the submit call. add_usage is called, so this happens before the response's tool calls run.

add_usage emits ExecutionDelta::Turn { usage: this response's own usage, call_ids }, then adds into the shared total under the lock and emits ExecutionDelta::Usage { usage: snapshot of the total }. The snapshot may already include tool_calls from earlier turns.

Stop-reason handling: PauseTurn, MaxTokens without tools, and a no-tool reply before the reminder all `continue` the loop. Refusal returns self.fail. A second no-tool reply ends with Ok and `usage = *self.usage.lock()`.

run_tools walks the calls in order. A call named submit_name goes to submit (not counted; on success the remaining calls get a 'Not run' result and the run returns TurnEnd::Submitted). Consecutive read-only tools (is_concurrent) run together with join_all, so their increments interleave under the mutex. Coordination tools run one by one, and every other tool runs one by one.

tool_end increments tool_calls first. After execution, for a Bash call whose command is_build_command against the profile's configured build and test commands, it adds out.duration_ms to build_ms. It then emits ToolResult with duration_ms (this per-call duration is not added to Usage).

On return from execute, the result carries `usage = *self.usage.lock()`: the sum of all responses and compactions plus the tool_calls and build_ms counters. Failure paths (`fail`, cancelled) copy the same mutex.

EngineHost::emit receives each delta. For Usage it computes usage_base + run total (usage_base is Usage::default() for a fresh execution and the stored row's usage when resuming a paused one), writes it with update_execution_usage, recomputes the session's cost as the sum of all executions' cost_usd plus the judge cost, and sends SessionUpdated. Every delta, including Turn, is appended to the activity log through append_activity.

After executor.run returns, the engine computes `usage_base + result.usage` and stores it with finish_execution. Cost reports then sum Usage per group and derive cache_reads_per_tool_call from tool_calls.

patterns.description: Run.usage is a single Arc<Mutex<Usage>> created in NativeExecutor::run and cloned into Run. Writer 1 is add_usage, called once per model response (and once per compaction) with the provider's usage. Writer 2 is tool_end, which bumps tool_calls and, for build and test Bash commands, build_ms. Every exit path of execute reads the same mutex into ExecutionResult.usage. On timeout or cancel, NativeExecutor::run reads the mutex after a CLEANUP_GRACE wait, so partial usage survives.
patterns.name: One shared Usage, two writers

patterns.description: tool_end emits ExecutionDelta::ToolCall and increments tool_calls immediately, before the invalid-JSON check, the policy check, the permission ask, and execution. A call that is denied by policy, denied by the user, or has invalid JSON is therefore still counted. The submit tool goes through the separate submit method, which emits ToolCall but never increments tool_calls, so a run's count excludes its final submit call. Coordination tools (SubagentAsk and the like) go through coord_tool -> tool_end and are counted.
patterns.name: Tool call counted at the start of tool_end, before any validation

patterns.description: All numeric fields are summed (tokens, cost_usd, tool_calls, build_ms). context_tokens is the exception: it is overwritten by the other value only when that value is nonzero, because it is the latest request's context size, not a total.
patterns.name: Usage::add merge rule

document.problem: The native loop keeps one run-wide Usage behind an Arc<Mutex<_>>. Token and cost figures arrive per model response and are added in; the tool_calls figure is incremented separately, one call at a time, inside the tool executor. The per-response (Turn) usage and the run total therefore carry different information: a Turn delta has tool_calls always 0 but lists call ids, while the running total has tool_calls but no per-call attribution.

submit.findings_summary: The native loop keeps one Arc<Mutex<Usage>> in Run. add_usage runs once per model response and once per compaction. It emits a Turn delta (that response's own usage and its tool call ids) and then a Usage delta (the running total). tool_calls is incremented at the top of tool_end, before the JSON, policy and permission checks, so denied calls count. The submit call goes through a separate method and is not counted. build_ms is added in tool_end for Bash build and test commands. EngineHost::emit rebases Usage deltas on usage_base (nonzero only for resumed executions) and persists them. After the run, the engine adds usage_base to the executor's result.usage before finish_execution.

docs.task: How an execution's usage reaches the store and the execution detail API, including the exported TypeScript types.

asks: How an execution's usage reaches the store
How it reaches the execution detail API
Which TypeScript types are exported for it

data_flow.step: Native executor: after each provider response, `usage = resp.usage` with `context_tokens = context_of(&usage)` (cost already computed by the provider client via `pricing::cost`). `add_usage` emits `Turn { usage, call_ids }`, adds the response to the shared running total, and emits `Usage { usage: total }`. Tool calls bump `total.tool_calls`; Bash build/test commands add `duration_ms` to `total.build_ms`.

Harness executor (Claude Code, Codex, Grok; not Antigravity): `usage_watch::follow` watches the CLI session file, builds `Usage` from `TranscriptReader::facts()`, replaces `tool_calls` with the live hook count, and emits `ExecutionDelta::Usage` when the value changed. No `Turn` delta is emitted by harness runs.

`EngineHost::emit` receives the delta. For `Usage` it adds `usage_base` (zero for a new run, the stored usage for a resumed one, Rule P2), then `WorkspaceDb::update_execution_usage` -> `Executions::set_usage` overwrites `executions.usage` (JSON) and `executions.cost_usd`.

Same call: re-sums `cost_usd` of all session executions plus judge cost into `sessions.cost_usd` and sends `EngineNotice::SessionUpdated`; then `append_activity` stores the delta (Usage and Turn alike) as JSON in `activity` and `EngineNotice::Delta` goes to WebSocket clients (`ws.rs`).

Run end: `executor.run` returns `ExecutionResult` with its own final usage (native: `*usage.lock()`; harness: `outcome::result` using the transcript facts). The runner computes `usage_base + result.usage`, calls `finish_execution` (writes `usage`, `cost_usd`, `status`, `submit`, `final_text`, `ended_at`), and appends `SessionEvent::ExecutionFinished { id, result }` to the event log. The fold keeps the result; `spent_usd` sums its `cost_usd` for the budget gate.

Crash and stop paths: `recover` and `stop_session_offline` read the stored view (`get_execution`) and put `view.usage` into the synthesized `ExecutionResult`, so usage stored by earlier deltas survives.

Detail API: `GET /api/executions/{id}` -> `get_execution` -> `Engine::execution` -> `WorkspaceDb::get_execution` -> `Executions::get` -> `execution()` row mapper (`usage: r.json("usage")?`). The engine then sets `has_terminal` and, for session executions, `view::decorate` fills the fold-derived fields; the handler ORs in `harness.has_terminal`. `usage` goes out unchanged as `ExecutionView.usage`. Cancel, skip, steer, withdraw, resume, and inspect return the same view.

Activity API: `GET /api/executions/{id}/activity?after=N` returns the stored `ActivityItem`s, which include every `usage` and `turn` delta; the browser folds them with `applyDelta` in `web/src/lib/events.ts`, which is where per-turn cost and an even per-call share of it appear.

Cost report: `Costs::report` selects `usage` JSON of executions since a time, groups by session, stage, agent, executor with `Usage::add`, and returns `CostReport` of `CostRow { key, executions, usage, cache_reads_per_tool_call }`.

TypeScript: ts-rs derives `Usage`, `ExecutionView`, `ExecutionResult`, `ExecutionDelta`, `CostRow`, `CostReport` into `web/src/api/gen/*.ts`; `web/src/api/types.ts` re-exports them; `web/src/api/client.ts` and the screens consume them.

document.problem: An execution's usage is one aggregate `Usage` struct per execution. It is built by an executor, passed to the engine through `ExecutionDelta::Usage` and `ExecutionResult.usage`, stored as a JSON column on the `executions` row, and served as `ExecutionView.usage`. Per-model-response usage exists only as `ExecutionDelta::Turn` rows in the `activity` table, with tool calls tied to a turn by id only. Nothing in the stored or served usage is broken down by tool. A change to the usage shape has to follow this whole chain, and `Usage` is `Copy` and built with struct literals in several crates.
document.scope: Task: how an execution's usage reaches the store and the execution detail API, including the exported TypeScript types. Covers the Rust path from the executors to the `executions` table and `GET /api/executions/{id}`, the activity log that carries usage deltas, the cost report, and the generated TS types plus the web code that reads them. It does not design any change, and it does not cover the web UI screens beyond naming which files read usage.
document.title: Execution usage: from executor to store, execution detail API, and TypeScript types

submit.findings_summary: Usage is a single aggregate `ostra_core::exec::Usage`. Native and harness executors report it through `ExecutionHost::emit` as `ExecutionDelta::Usage` and in the final `ExecutionResult.usage`. `EngineHost::emit` in `runner.rs` adds the resume baseline `usage_base`, writes it to `executions.usage` (JSON) and `cost_usd`, and appends the delta to `activity`. At run end `finish_execution` stores the final result and `SessionEvent::ExecutionFinished` logs it. `GET /api/executions/{id}` returns `ExecutionView.usage` read straight from the JSON column, and `view::decorate` does not touch it. `Usage`, `ExecutionView`, `ExecutionDelta`, `ExecutionResult`, `CostRow` and `CostReport` are `#[ts(export)]` and regenerate into `web/src/api/gen/`, re-exported by `web/src/api/types.ts`. No breakdown by tool exists in the stored or served data. `ExecutionDelta::Turn` (usage plus call ids) lives only in `activity`, and the browser splits a turn's cost evenly across its calls in `web/src/lib/events.ts`. `Usage` is `Copy` and built as struct literals across crates, so a non-Copy field would break it.
not_covered: Provider clients (ostra-providers anthropic.rs and openai.rs) that fill Response.usage and call pricing::cost
Judge and advisor usage (Services returns (Value, Usage); judge_cost per session)
Web screens that render usage (ExecutionScreen.tsx, MExecution.tsx, CostScreen.tsx, costTable.ts, mock fixtures)
Existing tests that build Usage struct literals, not checked for ..Default::default()
Harness LiveExecution and hook bridge that count tool_calls for harness runs (ostra-exec-harness live.rs)
